metadata.description: Azure App Configuration seed file for PharmaBackend. Import these key-values into your App Configuration store so that deployed environments source non-secret settings centrally. Connection strings and other secrets are intentionally excluded — route those through Azure Key Vault references.
metadata.excludedReason: No keys are excluded from App Configuration. All non-secret settings are stored here. Secrets are routed through Azure Key Vault references. No passwords are stored — Redis and PostgreSQL both authenticate via short-lived Azure AD access tokens obtained through Managed Identity (DefaultAzureCredential).
metadata.importCommand: az appconfig kv import --name <STORE_NAME> --source file --path .azure/configuration-migration.json --format json --profile appconfig/kvset --yes

keyVaultSecrets.note: No application secrets are stored in Azure Key Vault today. Both PostgreSQL and Azure Cache for Redis authenticate via short-lived Azure AD access tokens obtained through DefaultAzureCredential (Managed Identity on AKS, developer credential locally). There are no passwords, API keys, certificates, or bearer tokens in the source tree.

appCatFalsePositives.reason: Both flagged lines are fail-fast guard statements that throw InvalidOperationException when Redis:HostName or Redis:PrincipalId are missing at startup. The literal word 'secret' appears inside the user-facing error message text ('user-secrets') as a reference to the ASP.NET Core user-secrets provider — it is not a hardcoded secret value.

tags.notes: CDN base URL used by DbSeeder at startup. Override to an Azure Blob Storage URL when the image assets are hosted in Azure.
Fully qualified host name of the Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server, e.g. my-server.postgres.database.azure.com
Name of the PostgreSQL database on the Flexible Server.
Azure AD user or managed-identity display name configured as the PostgreSQL login. No password is stored — authentication is handled via OAuth 2.0 access tokens (Managed Identity).

Fully qualified host name of the Azure Cache for Redis instance, e.g. mycache.redis.cache.windows.net. Must be set to the FQDN before deployment. No password or access key is stored — authentication uses short-lived Azure AD access tokens obtained via Managed Identity (DefaultAzureCredential).

Object (Principal) ID of the Entra ID managed identity or user that has been granted access to the Azure Cache for Redis instance. This is the OID used as the Redis AUTH username in RESP3 token-based authentication. It is NOT a secret — store the OID of the UAMI (workload identity) configured in the AKS pod's serviceaccount annotation.
Refresh trigger. Increment this value in App Configuration to cause all registered settings to reload on the next incoming request (via UseAzureAppConfiguration middleware).
Development environment refresh trigger. Keep in sync with the unlabelled Sentinel when deploying dev-targeted configuration changes.
